  • 201:

    Sign in

    202:

    Everyone on the team signs in to Entire with Sign in with GitHub and authorizes the Entire GitHub App when prompted. You can do this at any time, before or after the next step.

    203:
    • 204:
  • 205:

    GitHub organization admin: import the repository

    206:

    A GitHub organization admin installs the Entire GitHub App on the organization by following the onboarding. Nothing repository-related appears for anyone in the team until this step is done.

    207:

    Sign-in order doesn't matter, but the repository and its sessions only show up after the admin has configured access.

    208:

    Once the admin has imported the repository, it appears for the whole team. No invites and no permission setup: access follows the GitHub collaborator list, so everyone keeps the same roles they have on GitHub.

    209:
    Changes can take up to an hour to sync. If the repository is missing from your list, ask your organization admin.
    210:
    • 211: 212:

    Next: install the CLI and start your first checkpoint (following section).

    213: 214: 215:
    216:
    217: 05 218:

    Start your first checkpoint

    219:
    220:
      221:
    1. 222:

      Install Entire, then enable it from your repository

      223:
      224:
      Shell
      225: 
      # macOS; see Resources for other platforms
226: brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
227: 
228: cd your-repo
229: entire enable --agent codex
      230:
      231: 232:

      Replace codex with your agent's integration name. Start a new agent session, ask it to make a focused change, and review the result.

      233:
      2. 234:
    2. 235:

      Commit the change

      236:
      237:
      Shell
      238: 
      git add path/to/changed-file
239: git commit -m "Build my first feature with Entire"
      240:
      241: 242:

      Choose yes if prompted to link the commit to session context.

      243:
      3. 244:
    3. 245:

      Inspect your checkpoint

      246:
      247:
      Shell
      248: 
      entire checkpoint list
249: entire checkpoint explain HEAD
      250:
      251: 252:

      A normal committed checkpoint needs both captured agent context and a Git commit. Full walkthrough

      253:
      4. 254:
    255: 256:
    257:
    258:
    259: 06 260:

    Turn on Trails

    Optional 261:
    262:

    You'll see Trails in action during our demo. To use it in your own repository:

    263: 264:
      265:
    1. 266:

      Request access from an Entiron after you onboard on Entire

      267:

      Trails is behind a feature flag. Once you've signed up, fill in the Trails access form and someone from the Entire team will enable Trails for you.

      268:
      2. 269:
    2. 270:

      Enable Trails in your repository

      271:

      Open your repository in Entire, go to Settings → General, and turn on Runners, Auto build on push, and Trails. This requires admin permission on the repository.

      272:
      Each Trail is currently backed by a GitHub PR for CI.
      273:
      3. 274:
    3. 275:

      Add the default Runners

      276:

      Runners evaluate each Trail and publish findings. From the repository root, run:

      277:
      278:
      Shell
      279: 
      entire runner setup -y
      280:
      281: 282:

      Then commit and push the generated .entire/ files.

      283:
      4. 284:
    4. 285:

      You or your agent: create a Trail and work normally

      286:

      Your coding agent already knows how to use Trails through the CLI, so just ask it to create one. Or run:

      287:
      288:
      Shell
      289: 
      entire trail create
      290:
      291: 292:

      Commit and push to the Trail branch as usual. The Trail updates automatically, Runners evaluate each push, and your team can review and merge from the Trail.

      293:
      5. 294:
    295: 296:
    297:
    298:
    299: 07 300:

    Continuous Memory

    301:
    302:

    Optional: only if you are building with Entire Graph/Brain.

    303: 304:
    305:

    AInstall and activate entire-graph

    306:

    You or your agents can install the entire-graph plugin. Activate it once per repository:

    307:
    308:
    Shell
    309: 
    entire plugin install graph
310: entire graph init-agents --repo .
    311:
    312: 313:

    The second command creates .entire/graph-agent.md with the agent instructions, and adds a short block to your AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md telling your agents to use entire-graph.

    314:

    Commit those three files so it applies to your whole team, then start a fresh agent session. You'll know it worked when your agent's first move is entire-graph search instead of a grep.

    315: 316:

    Start using entire-graph

    317:

    Restart the agent so it picks up the new instructions, then ask in plain language: Where is request routing implemented? The agent runs graph queries, reads the code the graph points to, and answers with citations.

    318:

    To see what it saved you, run:

    319:
    320:
    Shell
    321: 
    entire graph stats --repo .
    322:
    323: 324:

    It reads your Claude Code session transcripts, counts how many times your agent used the graph instead of grepping and reading files, and estimates the tokens it saved. For how entire-graph works, installation, and troubleshooting, see the Graph docs .

    325:
    326: 327:
    328:

    BInstall entire-brain

    329:

    Make sure the Entire CLI and entire-graph are installed first (steps above).

    330:
    Without entire-graph, setup reports the semantic index as unavailable; sessions, docs and facts still work. Without the Entire CLI there are no sessions to read, and entire-brain falls back to code, docs and Git history.

11: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
12: 
13: # Capture Sessions and Their Checkpoints
14: 
15: > Learn how Entire captures agent sessions and turns them into committed checkpoints.
16: 
17: Entire captures session context while you work, then creates a committed checkpoint when that context is linked to a Git commit.
18: 
19: ## How Capture Works
20: 
21: Checkpoint capture has two parts:
22: 
23: 1. [Agent hooks](/agents/overview) collect session context, including prompts, transcript, tool activity, changed files, and token usage when available.
24: 2. Git hooks link that captured context to a commit by adding an [`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer](/glossary#entire-checkpoint).
25: 
26: After the commit, Entire stores checkpoint metadata in your repository, in [its own Git ref or on the checkpoints branch](/security#where-your-data-lives) depending on the [storage backend](/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage). Your working branch stays clean.
27: 
28: ## Set Up Capture for an Agent
29: 
30: For a new repository, enable Entire with the agent you use:
31: 
32: ```bash theme={null}
33: entire enable --agent AGENT
34: ```
35: 
36: For a repository where Entire is already enabled, add another agent:
37: 
38: ```bash theme={null}
39: entire agent add AGENT
40: ```
41: 
42: You can see the supported built-in agents in [Agents](/agents/overview), or run:
43: 
44: ```bash theme={null}
45: entire agent list
46: ```
47: 
48: ## Commit After Agent Work
49: 
50: To capture agent-assisted work in a checkpoint:
51: 
52: 1. Start your agent from an Entire-enabled repository.
53: 2. Ask the agent to make a change.
54: 3. Stage and commit the change with Git.
55: 
56: ```bash theme={null}
57: git add .
58: git commit -m "Describe the change"
59: ```
60: 
61: If Entire detects recent agent work, it may ask whether to link the commit to the session context. Choose `yes` to create the checkpoint. Choose `always` if you want Entire to remember that preference for future matching commits.
62: 
63: ```text theme={null}
64: Entire: Active Codex session detected
65:   Last prompt: Add a user settings page...
66: 
67: Link this commit to session context?
68:   [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice):
69: ```
70: 
71: ## Link Future Commits Automatically
72: 
73: When the "Link this commit to session context?" prompt appears during `git commit`, choosing `yes` or `no` only applies to that one commit.
74: 
75: To link future matching commits in this repository without being prompted during `git commit`, set `commit_linking` to `always`.
76: 
77: Set `commit_linking` in one of these files:
78: 
79: * `.entire/settings.local.json` if this preference should only apply to you
80: * `.entire/settings.json` if this should be the team setting for the repository
81: 
82: ```json theme={null}
83: {
84:   "commit_linking": "always"
85: }
86: ```
87: 
88: ## Let the Agent Commit
89: 
90: Your agent can also create commits for you. For example, you might ask it to make a focused change and commit when it is done.
91: 
92: Entire still uses the Git hooks to link the commit to the captured session context. If the agent makes several commits in one session, each commit gets its own checkpoint.
93: 
94: ## Capture Multiple Commits from One Session
95: 
96: A single agent session can produce multiple checkpoints. This happens when a long session creates several commits, or when you split the agent's work into smaller commits yourself.
97: 
98: Each commit gets its own checkpoint ID. The checkpoints can share the same session context so you can still inspect the prompts, transcript, and work that led to each commit.
99: 
100: ## Capture One Checkpoint from Multiple Sessions
101: 
102: One checkpoint can also include more than one session. This happens when several agent sessions contribute to the work before you make a single commit.
103: 
104: In entire.io, those sessions appear together inside the checkpoint's Sessions tab. The checkpoint diff shows the combined change, while [session details](/guides/sessions/sessions-in-entire-io) show the context behind each contribution.
105: 
106: ## What Does Not Create a Checkpoint
107: 
108: Entire needs captured session context and a Git commit to create a normal committed checkpoint.
109: 
110: A checkpoint may not appear when:
111: 
112: * Entire has not been enabled in the repository
113: * agent hooks were not installed for the agent you used
114: * the agent did not change files in the repository
115: * no commit was created
116: * a GUI Git client could not find the `entire` command from its Git hooks
117: 
118: If a checkpoint is missing or did not link where you expected, see [Troubleshooting](/guides/sessions/troubleshooting).
119:

12: 
13: # Antigravity
14: 
15: > Capture Antigravity CLI prompts, session transcripts, recorded file changes, and token usage with Entire
16: 
17: Entire captures Antigravity CLI prompts, session transcripts, recorded file changes, and token usage, then links each session to its Git commits.
18: 
19: ## Before You Start
20: 
21: Install and authenticate [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/blog/introducing-google-antigravity-cli), and [install or update Entire](/installation).
22: Run `entire agent list` to make sure your installed build includes `antigravity`.
23: 
24: ## Add Antigravity
25: 
26: From a repository where you already enabled Entire, run:
27: 
28: ```bash theme={null}
29: entire agent add antigravity
30: agy
31: ```
32: 
33: If you have not enabled Entire in the repository, run:
34: 
35: ```bash theme={null}
36: entire enable --agent antigravity
37: agy
38: ```
39: 
40: Work and commit as usual. Entire captures the session in the background.
41: 
42: ## Hooks and Transcripts
43: 
44: Entire manages the `entire` entry in `.agents/hooks.json` and preserves other entries. The hooks capture turn boundaries and file changes. Entire reads prompts, responses, and tool calls from Antigravity's full JSONL transcript.
45: 
46: ## Token Usage
47: 
48: Antigravity supplies token usage through its title feed rather than its transcripts. When `agy` is on your `PATH`, Entire setup configures the `title` command in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` to pass that feed through `entire hooks antigravity title-tee`. Entire preserves an existing title command by wrapping it.
49: 
50: Token capture depends on this setting. Run `entire doctor` to check it, or rerun `entire agent add antigravity` to repair the setup. Removing the integration with `entire agent remove antigravity` also removes Entire's title wrapper and restores the previous command when present.
51: 
52: ## Verify Capture
53: 
54: Check tracking and the integration's configuration:
55: 
56: ```bash theme={null}
57: entire status
58: entire doctor
59: ```
60: 
61: See [Set Up an Agent](/agents/setup#verify-capture) to verify checkpoints and troubleshoot capture.
62: 
63: ## Limitations
64: 
65: * Entire does not display a tracking banner inside Antigravity. Use `entire status` to check capture.
66: * Entire does not yet support Antigravity subagent lifecycle hooks or attach subagent sessions to the parent checkpoint. Antigravity can still run subagents as separate conversations.
67: 
68: ## Resume and Import
69: 
70: To resume a recorded session on a branch, run:
71: 
72: ```bash theme={null}
73: entire session resume BRANCH
74: ```
75: 
76: Entire checks out the branch and restores the recorded session log when needed. In an interactive terminal, it asks whether to start the agent. Otherwise, it prints the resume command:
77: 
78: ```bash theme={null}
79: agy --conversation SESSION_ID
80: ```
81: 
82: Entire keeps an existing local session log by default. See the [`session resume` command reference](/cli-reference/session#session-resume) for flags and checkout behavior.

13: # Attach Sessions
14: 
15: > Link an existing agent session to a commit and checkpoint.
16: 
17: Attach a session when useful agent context exists, but Entire did not link it automatically.
18: 
19: ## When to Attach a Session
20: 
21: Use `entire session attach` when:
22: 
23: * hooks were not installed when the session started
24: * hooks did not fire
25: * a research session should be linked to the latest commit
26: * a completed agent review should be preserved as review context
27: 
28: ## Attach a Session
29: 
30: Attach reads an existing agent transcript, creates or updates a checkpoint, and links that context to the last commit.
31: 
32: ```bash theme={null}
33: entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT
34: ```
35: 
36: If the last commit already has an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, the session is added to that checkpoint. Otherwise, Entire creates a checkpoint and can amend the last commit with the trailer.
37: 
38: ## Attach without Prompts
39: 
40: Use `--force` when you want Entire to skip confirmation and amend the last commit:
41: 
42: ```bash theme={null}
43: entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT --force
44: ```
45: 
46: ## Attach a Review Session
47: 
48: Use `--review` when the session was an agent review of existing work:
49: 
50: ```bash theme={null}
51: entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent codex --review
52: ```
53: 
54: If the review used specific Skills, declare them with `--skills`:
55: 
56: ```bash theme={null}
57: entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent codex --review --skills review
58: ```
